notes.title: Languages of Shaola
notes.notes:
Numerous languages are used in Shaola, across the mainland and Everland in the Far East, beyond the Eastern Sea.

The [u]Old Tongue[/u], sometimes called the [i]Lost Tongue[/i], was the now-extinct language that existed in Shaola for millions of years. It consisted of the [i]High Tongue[/i] and the [i]Low Tongue[/i]. The former was used by scholars and the elite but it was not really a substantial or popular language. The latter, however, evolved from and was comprised of several ordinary languages derived from the High Tongue. The Low Tongues were spoken in the ancient towns and villages of Shaola. These communities ultimately grew away from each other, becoming mutually unintelligible.

Today, the Old Tongue is still remembered by the old giants and dragonriders but in the civilized communities, it exists only in rare ancient tomes. Most people on the mainland know no language other than the [u]Common Tongue[/u].

Although the Common Tongue has minor variations and regional accents, Southerners can communicate with Northmen without much difficulty.

Foreign tongues are taught in castles and by maesters or are brought and traded with immigrants, merchants, sellswords, and the like.

The foreign tongues are the seldom-used mother tongues that exist on the mainland as well as in Everland in the Far East, the mystical island across the Eastern Sea.

[i]Zorinese[/i] is the mother tongue spoken in the Zokang Kingdom and most of Everland, while [i]Old Zorinese[/i] is the tongue of seven of the nine ancient Green Tribes as well as other clans and indigenous inhabitants of the tropical forests of Everland.

Non-human tongues are the foreign tongues spoken by Elves and Dwarves. Both Wood Elves and High Elves speak [i]Ryllavian[/i], though Wood Elves are loyal to the original written form, while High Elves use a simplified version.

Dwarves speak and write [i]Kudorul[/i]; approximately 3% of the population uses [i]Old Kudorul[/i], an ancient language from millions of years ago.

notes.title: Orcs in Shaola
notes.notes:
In Shaola, most non-humans have been wiped out by Men's kingdoms and the Human Supremacy Alliance. The only surviving major races are [u]Orcs[/u], Elves, and Dwarves.

Orcs are one of the largest races of humanoid creatures. Each clan is composed of a large group of mindless brutal creatures who strive to burn and destroy for fun.

They are a brutish, aggressive, repulsive, and generally malevolent species and are usually pressed into the service of evil powers. Given that they are tall, big, and strong, Orcs are used as soldiers, slaves, and henchmen by greater villains.

They are miserable beings, hating everyone, including themselves and their masters, whom they serve out of fear. Orcs make no positive things; rather, they create devices to hurt and destroy.

Orcs, as well as ogres, trolls, and other goblins, have no languages of their own. They can’t write and must mimic Men’s Common Tongue for communication.

Most of the Orcish clans are led by Murlock the Slaughterer, a brutal and cunning leader who is also the strongest Orc fighter of all time.

Murlock claimed to unite all Orcs and fight for their freedom. He called for fellow Orcs to rebel and kill their masters. However, he has even bigger ambitions, vowing to unite all minorities (Orcs, Elves, Dwarves, and other beasts and monsters) and to declare war against the kingdoms of Men.

Murlock and the majority of Orcs reside in the North.

notes.title: Elves in Shaola
notes.notes:
In Shaola, most non-humans have been wiped out by Men’s kingdoms and the Human Supremacy Alliance (HSA). The only surviving humanoid races are Elves, Dwarves, and Orcs.

Elves are well known for their grace and mastery of magic and weapons such as the sword and bow. They are famously long-lived, with much longer lifespans than the average human.

Slightly smaller and shorter than most humans, Elves tend to be slender and graceful. This is reflected in a bonus to Agility and a penalty to Physical Defense.

Elves are divided into two distinct groups: [b]Wood Elves[/b] and [b]High Elves[/b].

Wood Elves are a reclusive race, partial to the old ways of life in the green world. They are conservatives who prefer old habitats in the woods, where they hide from Men and the HSA. Trees and flowers are their friends and wild beasts are their main source of food.

Wood Elves have produced some of the finest hunters and archers.

High Elves were once Wood Elves. However, as liberals, they eventually decided to live in cities with Men. They interact much more with other races and are the most open and friendly of their kind. They believe in peaceful coexistence.

High Elves travel everywhere, while most Wood Elves stay in the woods.

The decision of the High Elves’ ancestors to leave the green world for the shiny world of Men has always been controversial.

Some of them found success and happiness in serving humans, including in the Imperial Courts, and having great careers as bounty hunters or mercenaries. However, others have been miserable, suffering from depression and enduring unemployment and hunger. Some have sold themselves to slave owners in the Martia Kingdom. Others have been forced into slavery there.

High Elves have produced some of the most skilled swordsmen in the land.

Elves generally speak and write Ryllavian. However, Wood Elves use the original written form, while High Elves use a simplified version.

As a whole, Elves are the largest minority race in Shaola.

notes.title: Mysteries of Shaola: The Cave has been released on Steam
notes.notes:
Greetings fellow RPG lovers.

If you love Heroes of Shaola, you may enjoy the next game in this series: Mysteries of Shaola: The Cave.

The game has been released and is available now!

Mysteries of Shaola: The Cave is a role-playing game that brings mystery elements to the fantasy genre. Fight through the Kazen Kingdom and uncover the truth of the mysterious cave. Recruit a party of brave allies, fight orcs and other mythological creatures, explore Shaola in your search for adventure, treasures, and the truth. Discover secrets, build your legend and ultimately confront the corrupt force in this new chronicle of Shaola.

notes.title: Development update on the Shaola series
notes.notes:
It's been a long 2020! I thought now would be a good time for a development update since it's a brand new year and it's been awhile.

We all know 2020 was a tough year. We were hit with setbacks and development was stalled, but it's a brand new year and we're coming back in full force!

We're currently working on [i]Mysteries of Shaola: The Cave[/i]. It is a new chronicle of Shaola where you become Ice of Zuda Kingdom, the legendary investigator, one of the Magnificent Five. You fight through Kazen Kingdom and uncover the truth of the mysterious cave, discover dirty secrets, add to your legend, and ultimately confront the "evil" force. This role-playing game blends the genres of fantasy and mystery.

I have really enjoyed testing the game so far, and if you enjoyed [i]Heroes of Shaola[/i] for the characters and story, you'll definitely enjoy this one as well.

Also, as I'm making trailers for the new game, I made two for [i]Heroes of Shaola[/i] as well. I hope you enjoy watching them.

Eric

notes.title: The Shaola series
notes.notes:
Five years ago, we got together and started our research on parallel universes in fiction such as Middle-Earth, Neverland, Elfland, Discworld, and the rich worlds of A Song of Ice and Fire (Game of Thrones), The Witcher... as well as the great storytelling of Japanese fiction, notably manga and role-playing games. Afterward, we decided to write about the great stories in the world of Shaola.

With that approach, we focused on creating hybrid games that combine our favorite aspects of old school RPGs and JRPGs, while at the same time, removing those things some players didn't like, like random encounters and time-consuming grinding.

The Shaola project is the product of that research and ideas. Our games are not a copycat clone, which borrows ideas from old games, or games with a cheap nostalgia effect. This project is about utilizing some of the best ideas, features and characteristics from the oldies, remix and refine them, then combine and create a new and different type of enjoyment in a modern gaming era.

Shaola is a long-term project. It is a process of telling great stories about many appealing characters in different kingdoms and regions in Shaola. The gameplay in Shaola games will be based on the distinct story, characters, settings and environment of each title.

Hidden behind the beautiful high fantasy theme is the cruel world of medieval politics, as each character and faction has different motives and conflicts. Who can you trust?

Leonardo’s adventure is not a carbon copy of the Tolkien-esque RPGs in the 90s where you go on a heroic mission. You meet orcs, wizards, trolls, goblins, hobbits, and then you defeat some Dark Lords and win the game.

In this adventure, you are kidnapped into a foreign kingdom. You meet an unsecured prince, who is scheming to dispose of his own brother. The dark side of medieval politics comes out in full force.

We focus on blending historical fiction and medieval realism with epic fantasy.

A common theme in folk tales and mythology is the battle between good and evil, which does not always mirror the medieval world.

Old-time writers tend to oversimplify the struggle between good and evil into stereotypical clichés.

The Shaola series brings a measure of harsh realism to high fantasy. They introduce gray tones into a black-and-white universe.

Two permanent characteristics in every game in the Shaola series are: I. Fun gameplay that is easy to play. II. Advanced storytelling and building your enjoyment to the fullest. The story in each game will be enjoyable and on par with any adventure game or Visual Novel.

While this game is an RPG, one could say that it is an uncategorized game. It could belong to every subgenre out there, while you wouldn’t be wrong if you said it belonged to no subgenre at all.

It is a combination of many fun things that we’ve loved since childhood from our very first video game experience. The Shaola series is simply a tool to share the fun, excitement, enjoyment and delightful experience with you.

Changes in version 1.2.5:

[list][*] More user-friendly to casual players and non-RPG gamers.
[*] Arrow pointers have been added to a selection of outdoor maps, so that it is clearer on where to go to advance the story (*).
[*] Minor balancing to gameplay and battles.
[*] Further enhancement to scenes and dialogues.
[*] Minor revising to the relationship and interaction between characters. 
[*] Tutorial and instruction have been modified with more specific details.
[*] Sound effect have been improved, minor modification to music effect during important scenes or character’s reaction.
[*] A few story scenes and plots have been enhanced to bring each character to life.
[*] 2 minor tile issues have been fixed.
[*] Minor changes to a few items, weapons and armors.
[*] NPC dialogues have been enhanced.[/list]
* [i]In a certain parts of the game, arrow pointers won’t appear if they affect the fun of exploration. It is recommended that you don’t depend too much on the pointers. Don’t miss out on hidden areas and loot.[/i]
